newsitem.title: UK: Opposition says dozens arrested in Bahrain.
newsitem.headline: Opposition says dozens arrested in Bahrain.

text.p: A Bahraini opposition group said on Wednesday dozens of Bahrainis had been arrested this week, including youths and 18 people who were returning from a pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia.

The London-based Bahrain Islamic Freedom Movement said in a statement sent to an international news organisation that 29 people from seven Shi'ite Moslem villages had been detained, including teenagers.
They included Ammar Abdul-Fatah Khamis, 13, Jaafar Abdullah Jassim, 16, Mohammed Fakhr, 16, and Radhi Abbas Fardan, 17.
It said 18 people returning from pilgrimage had also been detained three days ago.
The group did not give the reason for the detentions. There was no immediate government confirmation.
Bahrain on Sunday denied a claim by the group that it had arrested 60 children in connection with political unrest in the Gulf Arab island state.
Members of Bahrain's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged sporadic protests since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms from the Sunni-led government.
At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds have been detained since the unrest began.
